items.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I think Charlie Parker was basic. Basic qualities.

ctx.x: I’m just trying to envision what it was like to play behind him.

He was very easy because he was a basic jazz guy. He was very, very basic. What I liked, he liked. I think there’s a certain element of jazzers that are basic guys, like Frank Rosolino. I think Charlie Parker was basic. Basic qualities. They didn’t have, they would take a tune and say here man, here’s the changes. This is what I want to hear. And I played with a lot of guys that are that way. And there’s nothing wrong with that either. It’s just that I’m saying he was more of a basic guy. He would leave it up to…

You’ve got some fascinating stuff there, from all your jazz to Elvis to Chet Baker. What is a recent album that you’re really happy with? Is there a recent album you’ve done that you’re really happy with? One of these? You can’t remember the titles, right?
